content.text:
Nature and science facts about the panda

The panda (giant panda) is a bear, but it eats almost only bamboo. Bamboo has little nutrition, so pandas spend a very large part of the day just eating. On their front paws they have a "fake thumb" — a modified wrist bone — that lets them grip bamboo like a hand while they eat. Their black-and-white markings are thought to help them hide in snowy mountains and in shade. Cubs are born very tiny and grow up under their mother's care, and because there are so few of them, the panda is a protected, endangered animal and a symbol of nature conservation.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. A panda is a bear, so why does it eat only bamboo?
A. It is a kind of bear, but it eats almost only bamboo. Since bamboo has little nutrition, it spends most of the day eating.

Q. What is a fake thumb?
A. It's a modified wrist bone that the panda uses to grip bamboo like a hand while eating.

Q. How can we observe at home?
A. Comparing your thumbs to the fake thumb, and talking about how the panda is "a symbol of nature conservation," both work well.
